title: Optimized Algorithms for Text Clustering with LLM-Generated Constraints
subcategory: LLM-generated must-link/cannot-link constraint sets + constrained k-means with penalties
problem: LLM-generated pairwise constraints are expensive to query and can be wrong; constrained clustering algorithms are not designed for noisy LLM constraints.
architecture: Constraint generation as sets (must-link sets via a coreset-inspired sampler, cannot-link sets via a skeleton structure) queried to an LLM; LSCK/LSCK-HC local-search constrained k-means with hard/soft must-link handling, confidence threshold and penalties for violated constraints.
llm_or_encoder: LLM constraint generator (DeepSeek R1 and V3 compared); Instructor-large and E5 embeddings
baselines: few-shot clustering constraint generation (Viswanathan et al.)
key_results: Tweet must-link constraints at the smallest ratio: Rand Index 100.00 with 99 queries vs 50.00 with 13070 queries for the pairwise baseline.
Clustering accuracy improves by more than 2% at a 40% constraint ratio on Tweet and CLINC (D).
strengths: More than 20x fewer LLM queries with equal or better constraint quality.
Complexity analysis of the algorithms (O(nk^2) for must-link handling).

limitations.text: As the number of constraints grows, the share of erroneous LLM constraints also rises; best results at about a 20% constraint ratio.
Constraint quality depends on the chosen LLM.
